utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Madam Registrar, I think before resuming the cross-examination of the witness Mr. Sabljica, I'd like to turn into private session in order to give a decision on a request made orally yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that "PS" disappeared from the screen. 1 1 That means that we now could escort Mr. Sabljica back into the courtroom. But I'll first ask the technical booth not to have his face on the video while he enters the Court, since facial distortion is one of the protective measures in effect. Mr. Usher, could you... Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Thank you. The Defence would just like to inform the Chamber concerning our conversation about the document 2172. Our learned friends informed us yesterday that it was on the 26th of November that they had provided us with the document that we were given yesterday. After a thorough search of all the documents in our possession, we just wish to notify the Chamber of the fact that we have not received such document. The document that we had under Number 2172 was an illegible document. In order not to waste this Honourable Chamber's time, I should kindly ask my learned friends from the Prosecution not to provide such false information to the Court. As for any misunderstandings that may have happened between the parties, I suggest that we try to clear up the issue amongst ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're talking about 2172, the photo series, or...?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it please you, Mr. President, without spending too much time on this, the Prosecution at no stage intends to proffer to the Court false information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And to make it quite short, I take it that if such statements are made, that these will be mistakes, if not true. I do not start with the thought that there would be any incorrect information given on purpose. That's my starting point for both parties. Would it ever turn out that it would be different, then of course we have a serious problem. But I do understand that the Defence says it's not correct information. I can't check it at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will check it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course you will check it. What I'd like to prevent is that, finally, this Chamber is sitting, hearing that false information is given, whether on purpose or not, that the other party says it's not true, et cetera, et cetera. If there's any such problem, I'd like you to ask the Prosecutor why he has given information which is not true so that he can at that very moment respond and say, well, it is true because of these and these reasons. And you check it again, and to solve these problems, at least to try to solve these problems first out of this courtroom, and only when both parties have tried to clarify where the misunderstanding is, and if finally one of the parties is really convinced that this Court is provided, on purpose, on important issues with false information, then of course we'll give it full attention. But first exchange your views, see where the miscommunication might be, and only if finally you will not resolve the problem, then come to the Court. Because then we can pay proper attention to it and not say, well, I hear you saying it's false, I hear you saying you didn't do it on purpose. I mean, it doesn't assist us very much in the conduct of the trial at this moment. If there's a great problem, we'll pay proper attention to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I entirely agree, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm happy to see both parties agree with what I said. Mr. Usher -- is there anything? Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just say that the statement having been put on the record just in respect to this issue, I will clarify it and provide the Court with very accurate information in respect to what was served and how many times these documents were served on the Defence. And I will do so after the next break, just for the record. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And if the parties might have difficulties in exchanging the views as I suggested to them, finally, I might -- or this Chamber might come to a position where we say these kind of objections, write them down, we'll see how they reach the Chamber, and not spend valuable time on it in Court. We have to make a clear distinction between those issues that are of importance to the trial and those issues that are mainly reflecting dissatisfaction, irritation, whatever you call it, because I want to make a clear distinction between these two. Mr. Usher, could you please lead in the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, excuse me, but with your permission, I should like to follow up on what you have just said regarding the following, and it is extremely important that we know for the purposes of the right of the Defence what has been done by the Prosecution in order to trace the evidence, physical evidence, that we have spoken about, that is the fragments of the shell. We should like to ask the Prosecution how far they have gone in that search, because a number of questions that we wanted to ask of this witness will simply not be -- it will simply not be possible to ask them because we have been prevented. I mean, we practically have been prevented from using this possibility. And I should like to hear Mr. Stamp to tell us how things stand in respect of this issue so as to give us a general idea of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, is there any new information, because we discussed the matter a couple of times over the last few days?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, we have discussed it quite a few times over the last few days, and it was indicated that the Prosecution would give some response in respect to that matter and the matter of the orders, or to give whatever additional information that we have. Could we do so after the next break? We are still trying to get whatever information we can put together in a comprehensive package. And one of the sources of that information would only be available this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I think at this moment, especially the shrapnel, the -- well, the search for the present location of the shrapnel that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're quite right. That is in relation to Rule 96(ii)(A). The Defence is not in a position to determine its stand because we do not dispose of these very important elements, this very important evidence. If this issue continues, I think it will be to the detriment of General Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're referring to 96(ii)(A) but --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. No. I said 90(H)(ii).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there any additional information, just about the shrapnel, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We have not been able to locate the shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We have done everything we can to obtain whatever artifacts which remain or which were collected. The evidence before the Court is that many of these things were lost or possibly thrown out over the years when the building moved, or when changes were made. We have made requests; we have repeated these requests. We have sent missions. We have asked for searches, and we have obtained what we can. We continue to make requests, and we continue to try to locate whatever artifacts we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where there any new initiatives during the last few days?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, but I would ask if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Without results. So at this very moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, without results.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as I indicated before, the Defence, of course, also could try to locate the shrapnel. What initiatives have been taken by the Defence in that respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, following the suggestions made by the Chamber, I stated that I would personally write to the authorities. However, it is not very simple. I'm trying to identify the relevant authority that might help us. Maybe we will use diplomatic channels because it is evident that if a humble lawyer should write directly to the MUP, I don't think he can expect a prompt answer. So I'm trying to explore the best possible ways to approach the issue, to identify the relevant authorities. I will expect some answers next week, but I have to tell you right away that I'm not harbouring too much hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, for your information. Before I ask the usher to bring the witness into the courtroom, may I urge both parties to use their time as efficiently as possible, because we all know that since preparations have been made for the videolink for next week, that those witnesses waiting here, of course it would be a pity if we would have to send them back and recall them at a later stage. So may I especially at this very moment ask for the utmost efficiency by both parties. Mr. Usher, would you please bring in Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Sabljica. May I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you made last Monday. The cross-examination by Ms. Pilipovic will now continue. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, before we adjourned, we spoke about an incident which you, as a member of a team of the Sarajevo CSB, attended and took part in the conduct of investigating activities. You told us that the shrapnel was collected by Mr. Sead Besic?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally see the shrapnel in question in the archives of your service, that is, the public Security Services Centre?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Besic take photographs of that shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him taking photographs, and I presume that he was also taking photographs of the shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When and where was that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the on-site investigation. As we visited the scene, he photographed the traces of the explosion, including the shrapnel that we found on the site.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show the witness Document D61. It is a set of photographs of shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. Mr. Usher, could you assist.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, frankly speaking, it could be a photograph of any similar case, so I cannot confirm with certainty that this is the shrapnel from Markale market.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in a position to see them lined up in this way when your colleague, Mr. Besic, took photographs of them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just inquire through the Court if the document he is looking at could be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, I should like to ask you to put it on the ELMO so that we can all see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him arrange the shrapnel in this manner. I saw him taking photographs of the shrapnel on the location while they were still on the market at various locations around the explosion spot. He did this probably later on, so I presume that this photograph was taken somewhere in the offices of the crime laboratory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether the shrapnel, together with the tail-fin, were ever sent for analysis?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any such knowledge, but I know that if the adequate procedure was followed, they must have been sent for analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sabljica. Mr. Sabljica, you told us that as a team member of the on-site investigation, you were present when the incident took place on the 4th of February in Dobrinja. Can you tell us, in relation to this incident, in what capacity were you there as a team member?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there in the capacity of a ballistics expert. I was one of the ballistic experts team that was led by the investigative magistrate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief, you explained to us that you proceeded to the analysis of site 1 and 2, and that you found some stabilisers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your written report, the on-site report, states that on the 4th of February in Dobrinja, two shells hit, and that the calibre of these mortar shells were 120 millimetres. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to us how is it that an official report contained that -- or states that there were three shells if the analysis was not carried out?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigating magistrate, Mr. Zdenko Eterovic, insisted upon the fact that we should also mention a third shell that we had not analysed and that had hit a religious building that was situated right behind the square. He had gone with the operative to examine the site in question. This is the reason why we stated that fact in the report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you consider that it is sufficient to inscribe information that you obtained from a nonprofessional that a shell of 120 millimetres hit? Do you think this information is sufficient to include it in an official report?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: My personal decision is that an omission was made. The judge really insisted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We were able to see on pictures that we examined in Court that right next to the site where the shell fell, that there were some maps placed. Could you tell us who placed those maps around those impact sites?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The maps were placed by Mr. Zlatko Medjedovic and myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how did you go about placing these maps? Did you have to do something special? What are the measures that you take in order to place these maps? How do you determine where to place these maps?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map has to be placed in the direction of the north, so we have to first establish the north, and then we have to identify the magnetic north with the help of a compass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that you can make a mistake when you place the maps in such a way?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is always possible. There's always a difference of a plus/minus 5 degrees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is the difference in terms of degrees between the north and northeast?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the difference in terms of degrees between the difference -- in the difference between the north and northeast? What do you read on the compass when you say that you determined the north?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the compass, between the north and the east, the angle that is shown is 90 degrees. So between north and northeast, the difference should be 90 degrees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to us, why did you and Mr. Medjedovic, when you were on the site, why did you not determine the angle of descent of the two shells at the spot where you found the stabilisers?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was never part of our on-site investigation. That was not part of our task to determine from where the shell fell, but only the direction. So we never really had to evaluate the descent angle, the angle of descent.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show a set of pictures. It is the Prosecution's Document P2247, and it's pictures that were taken or relate to the incident of the 24th of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, those are the two pictures, P11, pictures on which you have placed arrows that show the direction from which the shell fell.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... or Prosecution Exhibit P2247?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the Document P2247A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, please look at picture number 5 first, and then I would like you to examine picture number 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would just pause one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, you refer to 2247. That is a set of photographs. And when asked for a specification whether you'd like to have 2247 or 2247A, you said you'd like to have 2247A, which is a report. I take it that you want to show to the witness 2247, the set of photographs. Yes. Yes, that's an existing exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm terribly sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please then proceed. Would you please then put the photographs on the ELMO, Mr. Usher. So the photographs that were on the ELMO. And may I ask the booth --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, would you please look at picture number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The French interpreters are stating that they no longer have a transcript. So I don't know if they are following the transcript and interpreting from the transcript, but I would like to ask the technical booth to do something. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that the transcript channel on our screens gives a "no signal" sign. On our laptops, however, we have a transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the parties at this very moment use their laptop transcript, which is the -- the interpreters have no laptops. Perhaps we first wait, because the interpreters also need to have their facilities working. I think we have to have some patience. Yes, I see that on all the screens I can overlook from here, that the transcript is again on our screens, and it shows us that high-tech is beautiful as long as it functions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, please take a look at picture number 5, first.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the east indicated on this picture on the map, and were you able to determine if in that direction you could place the building Energoinvest?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it written under there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please take a look at picture number 11. We can also see that there is a map placed. There's also a compass and an arrow. Underneath, we can see the following inscription: direction, east northeast. We can also read that in that direction, the building Energoinvest Lukavica is located. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us the following: If one says that a shell that has 120 millimetre calibre and that it flew from the direction of the north and that the second shell was -- or arrived from the east, we said that there is a certain angle of difference in the angle, and we have established that there's a difference between the east and northeast, so there is a difference in angle between the two. And here, we see that we're talking about the east, east-north, if you will. How were you able to determine in both cases that the shells came from the direction of the Energoinvest building, that the axis was from there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The complex of this building Energoinvest was just an orientation point. One shell flew from the east and the other one from the northeast, so there was a certain difference in degrees. And we did not put that down between the north and the east, so their points actually concurred somewhere around the Energoinvest building, and this is what I drew, actually. I made a sketch of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me to say that the difference between north and northeast, difference in angle, is 45 degrees?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's somewhere between 0 and 45 degrees, so it's one of these angles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you consider your conclusion that both shells came from the direction of the Energoinvest building correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat that the Energoinvest building was only considered to be as an orientation point. We only mentioned that building as a supposition. We were never able to determine that the shell was fired from that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if, based on these facts for which you stated they are erroneous and that they are only orientational points, why is it hat in your reports you wrote down that those shells came from the position of the aggressor?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just ask for clarification of that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Clarification of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would it be possible to confront the witness with the exact part of his report, or the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the report from the forensic department, this is a report dated February 4th, 1994, bearing number 234-94. For this report, it is possible for us to show it to the witness, if you will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you read the line with which you would like to --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. In order to be more efficacious, I will read line: "On the 4th of February, 1994, at 11.25, the aggressor fired from their positions in Lukavica and fired three mortar shells of 120 millimetres calibre in the Dobrinja neighbourhood on the street of Oslobodilaca Sarajeva."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, do you know if this is an official report, and do you know if those three shells, in fact, flew in from the direction of the aggressor? Was this, in fact, an official report? Do you know this?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the first time that I hear of this report. What I wrote in my report is quite different. This is not what I'm stating in my own report, and I can only confirm what I wrote. I do not know who wrote this at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, thank you. Can you tell us if concerning this incident that took place on the 4th of February, 1994, in Dobrinja, do you know if the UNPROFOR was informed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, and can you tell us, if the UNPROFOR members later, after your on-site investigation with the team in question, do you know if they proceeded to do some measurements and if they had received a report regarding this incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not know this, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sabljica, I would like to ask you a few questions relating to an incident that took place on the 22nd of January in Alipasino Polje. Would you be able to tell us when did you arrive on the scene?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 2.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all the team members arrive at the same time, or did you come there individually at different times?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the investigating magistrate was about 10 minutes late, so we waited for him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what were the weather conditions that day? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was snow on the ground, but it was not snowing, and I do not know if it was a clear day or it was an overcast day. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived on the scene, while you were waiting for the investigating judge, did you find or did you see the stabiliser there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. For those two 82 millimetre shells, we did not, except for one shell for which allegedly it was said that it fell on the roof and that has 120 millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, regarding the 82 millimetre shell that you recorded on Cetinjska Street, which has a different name today, it's Goethe Street, do you know how many casualties there were caused by this shell?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that in the report, we can see that there were five casualties, but that's relating to this second incident that occurred in front of the number 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't really remember this incident clearly?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you would allow me to consult my report, then I would be able to tell you with certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us and do you know if on Rade Koncara and in that general area, which is known under the name of Alipasino Polje, do you know if there were any military installations around that area or in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find out perhaps later on that there were some police -- some reserve police stations there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just told us that on Goethe Street number 3, an 82 millimetre shell hit at that spot. Can you tell us and confirm to us if on Klare Zetkin Street number 4, there was also an 82 millimetre shell that fell?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps I missed it, perhaps there's some problem with the translation. I don't have it where he said anything about Goethe Street number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think recently -- since there has been a change of names, that at least one of the things that has been said, but I'm not quite sure whether it was Ms. Pilipovic or the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: She said it. That's not evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Ms. Pilipovic, would you first seek confirmation whether your interpretation of the new name of the street is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, can you tell us if the street that used to be Cetinjska number 3 is now called Goethe Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I really don't know what the new name is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if the street that used to be called Klare Zetkin is now called Bosanska?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know this either. I could not confirm this to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I think you're perfectly right, it was not the testimony of the witness. But, of course, there could be hardly any confusion if Ms. Pilipovic says that a street with a different name is now called Goethe Street. And if she asks about Goethe Street, then of course I understand that she refers to the street of which the name was given before. So I would say that although you're perfectly right, there would be hardly any misunderstanding possible. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I really didn't want to waste any time, so I didn't really show the map of the city of Sarajevo. But I checked on the map, and I realised that these streets have changed names, and that Klare Zetkin now changed the name to Bosanska, and that Cetinjska Street changed its name to Goethe Street, but I will, for the purposes of this day today or trial today, use the old names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do expect that there's no intention whatsoever, and there would be no confusion. But if you use the names of the streets used in the reports as they were at that time, then I think -- but I can imagine when you prepared your cross-examination that you used the other street names. I'd prefer if you used the same names of the streets as the witness did before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. I was just suggesting that we could agree upon it. But she also could use the previous names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think let's continue, because what Ms. Pilipovic thinks is the Goethe Street is the street mentioned by the original name as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think she really means Gatiova, G-a-t-i-o-v-a, not Goethe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's Goethe, the German writer. That's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. Your Honour, I did say that I was going to use the previous names of streets just to avoid any confusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, on the 22nd of January, did you carry out an on-site investigation regarding Cetinjska number 3 Street, and did you also go to the site of the Klare Zetkin Street number 4?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also carry out an on-site investigation for which it was determined that a 120 millimetre shell landed on the Rade Koncara Square?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your report that you read to us yesterday which is, by the way, illegible and which was also signed by the late Borislav Stanko, did you confirm therefore in this report that on that day two 82-millimetre shells landed and that there was also another 120-millimetre shell that was -- that fell?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, during your on-site investigation which took place on those two sites, in order to determine the direction from which the shell arrived, did you use the same means in order to establish this? And we've talked about these means in length.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we always use the same method.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also place a town map on the spot which you marked with arrows, and did you have a compass on that occasion as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we used the usual -- the same procedure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you cleared up the impact location during this particular on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That job is normally done by crime technicians, but I don't remember seeing them do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When this incident happened, who was the crime technician, or who were crime technicians? If you want to use the name of a protected witness, you should perhaps want to use letter "Q."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Witness Q, you're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm a bit surprised that a witness would know about exactly the pseudonyms given to other witnesses, but is there any misunderstanding possible? If not, please proceed. But you'll understand that the witness should not be aware of any protective measures taken in respect of other witnesses. But finally, if this satisfies both parties, then it's all right as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that the witness normally should not know; however, I think that yesterday he was in the courtroom when we referred to this particular witness, so he is aware of the fact that he is a beneficiary of some protective measures. That's why I think he reacted this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we located the source of knowledge for this witness, but I'd like to tell you, Mr,. Sabljica that by misfortune you became aware of the identity of a witness which is called "Q" in this courtroom. You're not allowed under whatever circumstances to give this information to any person outside this courtroom. I just wanted you to know that you're under an obligation to keep this a secret, as it is for everyone in this courtroom. Yes? Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you now tell us what particular forensic measures or steps were taken by Witness Q, apart from the fact that he took photographs?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with the long-established procedure, the crime technician was in charge of preparing the scene for the purposes of carrying out further analysis which is then done by us, ballistics experts. At that moment, I was not supervising him because, after all, he's a well-experienced technician. But I know that he enabled us to carry out our on-site investigation without major difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show the witness at this point Prosecution Exhibit 2172, the set of photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Document Number P2172.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, would you first of all look at the photograph number 1 on this document, please. Can you confirm for us that the arrow indicates the explosion site in Cetinjska number 3 on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us why on this occasion you did not photograph -- you did not take any photograph at the moment you put the town map and the compass on the site?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact explanation, but I remember that the technician took those photographs as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in a little bit so that we can see the exact location where the shell landed, where the arrow is, please. It's not a very clear picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, have another look at the photograph, please, and tell us whether you can confirm whether the impact point and the area surrounding it is especially visible, and that it is actually a cleared-up portion of the area? I am referring to the area which surrounds the impact point.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly, do you want to ask me whether this was properly cleaned up?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, I want to ask you whether anyone cleaned the site, and is it the usual procedure prior to taking photographs of the impact point?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is the usual procedure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now have a look at photograph number 2, please. You confirmed that this photograph also depicts the impact point in Cetinjska number 3?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please have a closer look at the photograph and the direction of the arrow towards the very edge of the photograph and tell us what part of the neighbourhood can be seen on this photograph, that is, the buildings that we can see in the distance. And is it a mountainous, hilly area, and if you know, tell us what area it is precisely?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is the edge of the Mojmilo neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that the Mojmilo hill is in the same direction?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the very edge, the first slopes of Mojmilo hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to whether during that period of time, in 1994, the hill was under the BH army control? Were BH army troops there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the front line at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was the front line? Actually, how far apart those lines were?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean between the BH army and VRS?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, you told us that your internship lasted until the end of 1993 and that you didn't have to pass an examination -- that you didn't take a test. Is that the reason why you didn't sign the report of the incident which took place on the 22nd of January? Is that the reason why it was Mr. Stanko who signed the report in question?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in that capacity at the time have authority to sign records of investigation? When I say "record of investigation," I refer to ballistics records of investigation, or was it the case that more experienced colleagues signed such documents?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had the authority to sign the record from the beginning of December 1993. But in this case, this was done by the late Stanko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you the authority to sign such records? Did you have a written permission, written authority, to sign such records?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the then head of the forensics department who gave me such permission, Mr. Nedzad Zekic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sabljica, can you tell us whether it is important for the purposes of a ballistics analysis to measure the distance between the impact point and the closest buildings?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally, this is always done, but it is for the purposes of doing the reconstruction of the event pursuant to a request made by an investigating magistrate or some other authority. The impact point is always taken with respect to some fixtures, some buildings, or other similar facilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you telling us that it is important for the purposes of a ballistics analysis to measure the distance between the impact point and the closest facilities?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it has nothing to do with the analysis of the incoming path of the shell. It is in order to satisfy the usual requirements of an investigation report that this is done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring specifically to the 22nd January incident. Did you take any such measures on this occasion, that is, did you measure the distance between the impact point? We saw that you did so in Cetinjska number 3, but did you also take measurements of the distance between the impact point and the nearest building?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you'll allow me to have a look at my report, perhaps I will be able to confirm your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you read out the report for us. I don't want to have it read once again. I'm referring to the same report.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally, it is the usual procedure that we sort of fix the impact point with respect of a building, but I don't remember that we took any specific measurements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the course of your work in the MUP, that is, the public security centre, did you know that there was a factory for mine production at Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since we were able to confirm from your report that on the 22nd of January two shells landed, two 82-millimetre shells and one 120-millimetre shell, do you know what the report was, the one that was made by the crime technicians in respect of this particular site?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I haven't read this report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put to you the 22nd January report --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence would like to tender the report concerning the 22nd of January incident as an exhibit, and we would like to show it at this point to the witness. I will read the relevant portion of the report in respect of which I need an answer. The relevant report has been translated into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you'd -- have you prenumbered the report, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. D67.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the English translation will then be D67.1. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think if you tender the document, it could be given to the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just comment that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If perhaps the Court could ask the witness to be careful not to put the document on the ELMO unless directed because there's a name on it we perhaps don't want --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If we perhaps -- I haven't read it yet. Let's start to keep it from the ELMO until we have a ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These forms and the method of writing such forensic reports on on-site investigations, are they the same as the ones that your service uses? Is it the same kind of document that you have to fill out after an on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and they are filled out by crime technicians or forensic experts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that there was a forensic expert at the scene together with you on that day. After number 4, can we read on this document that on the 22nd of January, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around 13.50, from the direction of Nedzarici west, two mortar shells fell, each of 120 millimetres, in Klare Zetkin number 4, and another one in Cetinjska number 3.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the report says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having in mind the answers that you have so far provided concerning the identification of mine calibres, shell calibres, can you confirm that this report is consistent with what you were able to establish? Let me just remind you that you testified that the shells in question were 82 millimetre shells.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree. What has been written here by the crime technician is not accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, can you confirm for us whether it is acceptable for Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. an investigation team conducting a visit of a crime scene, especially in cases of such serious incidents with grave consequences, to make such arbitrary and unconfirmed reports? Is this an acceptable practice? In particular I'm referring to the fact that there are two different reports here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can, that is, I can confirm that it is an unacceptable practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sabljica. Will you please look at photograph number 5 at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we still talking about 2172, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the set of photographs, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2172, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have in front of you, Mr. Sabljica, photograph number 5.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the distance is between the spot which is marked with an arrow where you established a shell had landed and the nearest entrance of this building? What is the distance between the impact point and the building?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 10 metres to this alley, this passage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the nearest steps?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 5 to 6 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that the location at number 4 in Klare Zetkin Street is a location where the shell landed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us about the effects of this 82 millimetre shell. What were the consequences; that is, how many casualties were there in this particular incident, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report states that five persons were killed in this incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you take photographs of this location? You did so after the incident. You said that you arrived at the scene around 2.00, 2.00 p.m., and that the incident took place at around 11.00 a.m. So is it, what, two hours after the incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Again, I might have missed something. Did the witness say that the incident took place at around 11.00?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please locate the source, Ms. Pilipovic. It's not in my recollection. I'm not saying yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we will check.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, do you know when, at what time, this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you let me look at the report, I can tell you the exact time, but I think it occurred at about 11.00. We can check.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have the relevant record in front of me. I can show it to the witness. However, I cannot see from the record of the on-site investigation that the time is indicated. What we have here is at about 1.15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it then 1.15 or 11.00?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then it must be at 1.00 p.m. and 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you arrive at the scene?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: An hour later, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague is telling me that this would be the convenient time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Stamp, you're on your feet. I thought you would --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. I would have liked to address the Court on a certain matter. I will do so. As I indicated earlier, I accept Your Honours' order that certain matters should be dealt with between counsel, and we will do so in future. However, something was stated on the record, and I just wish to put on the record that in June 2000, the coloured documents were delivered to Mr. Kostic for the Defence, and he signed for it. Thereafter when counsel, Ms. Pilipovic, became involved, she indicated that she had problems in the transfer of documents. And on the 3rd of March, 2001, the coloured copies were delivered to her and she signed for it -- the 1st of March, and they were signed for. Subsequently, the documents, not coloured copies, were again disclosed to the Defence. So coloured copies have been disclosed more than once to the Defence, and we will produce receipts if called upon to do so. I say this just for the record in respect to this. In the future, we hope to communicate with counsel and deal with these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what the Chamber hopes that will be done as well. If there is any dispute as to whether documents have been given to the Defence, of course you'll first show each other the receipts, the dates, et cetera. And only if then finally it turns out that any obligation has been neglected by one of the parties, and if this would be of any substantial influence on the trial, then of course this Chamber will be glad to hear about it. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the Court's indulgence, just a second, Your Honour. The colour documents were received by me, however, not in respect of this incident. I received the documents for the 5th of February and the 22nd of February [sic]. I simply see no reason why I would have stated anything different had I received the document. But I'm sure that I have not received these specific documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the first thing the parties now will do is to see whether the information about the delivery of colour documents was information concerning the same photographs or different photographs. If a serious problem remains, I'll be glad - and I'm sure that my colleagues are also glad - to hear so. If no serious problem remains, we would love not to hear about it any more. We'll have a break until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. After I read at least part of the correspondence and just very briefly -- I see, Mr. Ierace, you appear in Court. Is there any specific reason? Not that you're not welcome in this courtroom, but I expected that Ms. Pilipovic would resume the cross-examination of the witness. Is there anything you want to bring to the attention of the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On Tuesday morning, Mr. President, I said that this morning, Thursday morning, I would report back briefly in response to the two questions that you posed, namely, whether the Prosecution has disclosed to the Defence all of the orders which we hold of the 1st Corps, and secondly, whether we have disclosed all of the orders which we hold from the main staff to all of the corps including the 1st Corps, that is, orders which apply to all of the corps. The answers to those two questions I can now provide, together with some brief information in relation to the shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, the shrapnel -- I'm a bit hesitating to do this in the presence of the witness. So I don't know whether you stay with us for the next one hour and a half. If so, I would rather do it then at the end. How much time would it take you, so that perhaps we first continue with the witness, and then do it at the end before the next break. Would that be convenient to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President, I could return, say, five or ten minutes before the end of this session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That would be approximately -- let's say if you would return at 12.20, approximately. I would rather not interrupt, if not necessary, and send out the witness again. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. Ierace. Ms. Pilipovic or Mr. Piletta-Zanin, who is going to resume the cross-examination of Mr. Sabljica?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is going to be my colleague, Ms. Pilipovic, but I just wanted to reply that yes, we are very agreeable to your suggestion, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we talked about picture number 5 before the break. Is this picture near you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at photo number 5. You told us already what the distance was between the place where the shell hit and the entrance or the passage. Could you explain to us the area that surrounds the building that doesn't seem to be damaged from the shell, how do you explain this fact that a shell landed at that site and that it did not damage this particular building that we see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building is in the opposite direction of the direction from which the shell arrived, and the shrapnel effect on that side was less important. So I think that from the angle from which the picture is taken, we cannot really see very clearly that there was some damage done to the building that was situated in the direction of this arrow, that is, the opposite side of this one. I believe that the crime scene technician made an omission because he did not take a picture of the facade and the surrounding area surrounding this particular staircase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sabljica. Regarding the question I just asked in relation to the damage, could you please take a look at picture number 1. Can you tell us the effect caused of the shell that fell around this? Can you tell us why is it that there was no damage caused to those cars?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The picture does not depict very clearly the crater. I cannot really orient myself with respect to the crater. But those cars were damaged previously already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sabljica, would you be able to tell us if the CSB was under the control of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were working at the CSB, did you know if there were some special units within the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which are those special units for which you know that they existed? Did they have any particular names?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of the special unit of the MUP, the commander of this unit was Mr. Vikic. And I also know that there was a special unit of the CSB called Lasta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if there were some special units called Seva within the MUP, and those units would be sniping units and special -- there was also a special unit called a Delta within the MUP. Are you aware of the existence of these two units?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of these two units through the media, but only after the conflict had ended already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what did you know about the Seva unit? What role did this unit have from what you found out later on?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a special unit, nothing else. I did not read anything more in the Nasi Dani paper. It was a special purposes unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were working at the MUP, were you aware of the fact that on the area of Sarajevo, in the city of Sarajevo that was under the control of BiH, that there were some special prisons, and by this I mean special prisons destined for Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that there was a prison in the old Viktor Bubanj barracks, and there were some other -- everybody was actually at that prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this ends my cross-examination with regards to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I did understand that you divided your cross-examination, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon or good morning, Witness. I have a few questions for you. I will try to be as brief as possible to save time, of course. You have stated yesterday, Witness, that for a certain period of time, you were an active soldier in the Sarajevo army, the government army, as it was called. Do you confirm this fact?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us, when were you an active member of the army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 28th of April, 1992. Up until mid-June 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this answer. So therefore, you were probably -- you had a weapon, and if so, what kind of weapon were you handed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the means that were available on the line. Sometimes it was a hunting rifle. Other times it was a semi-automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Please tell us, did you use this weapon or those weapons during the period of time during which you were an active soldier or you were under the banner of this army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. While on the defence line, if we were attacked, we had to respond to the fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for this answer. You have also stated that there were some exchanges of fire almost every day. May I deduce -- deduct from this answer of yours that you frequently had to use your weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that often because it also often happened that while I was on duty, while I was doing my shift, that there were no shootings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And against whom were you using those weapons exactly, or this weapon?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Against the enemy at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, can you confirm that each time you shot, you were able to target the target? You were able to hit the target?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I could not confirm this. It is quite impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. Witness, as a ballistics expert, can you tell us if that is the case that the ricochet phenomenon could occur, theoretically?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this answer. Witness, it is, therefore, absolutely possible that some lost bullets, stray bullets, could have been shot by you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is absolutely possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this answer, Witness. And tell me if I'm mistaken, it is also possible that such a stray bullet could have hit people or persons that you were not particularly targeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That possibility always existed, but we were always on the lines that were confronting the army and not anybody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. I do thank you for this answer. Witness, are you familiar with the factory called Zrak?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know where that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us if you know, first of all, where was this factory situated, and what it was producing?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is still there where it was at that time. It's Buca Potok, and it was for the military purposes, used for military purposes in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. To be more precise, this factory produced products for the military industry. Could you tell us what type, what was the specialisation? This factory specialised in what precisely, if you can tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was optical devices that was serving the purposes of the JNA, the former JNA, optical sights.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you say that those products, that it was used for the JNA army, whatever they were producing. Was it only used for the JNA? Were they producing only for the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not know what their policy was, but in the former Yugoslavia, they were only making products for the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I see, former Yugoslavia, yes. Mr. Witness, as of the month of April 1992, who had the control of that factory, what party, what belligerent party?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer, Witness. In the month of April 1992, the factory, was it still operational?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. What happened in the following month?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, this factory, was it not making targeting implements destined to be placed on barrel of -- rifle barrels?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they had that programme. They were producing -- they were making those implements, so these optical devices that you would place on a sniping rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I now heard exactly what I had not understood clearly earlier. So we are talking about rifles with sights, and that could always be used, of course, by snipers?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was part of their production programme for the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you just told us that in April of 1992, the factory was still operational. Do you know what happened with the stocks produced by this factory?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. You would have to ask somebody who was actually working at the factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we will try to find somebody who worked at the factory. Thank you very much, Witness, for this suggestion. Now, do you know if units, sniping units that existed in Sarajevo on the side of the so-called government army, had those devices, those optical targeting devices?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you, Witness. I really do. However, do you know, Witness, if those isolated units, sniping units, were they within a military structure? And I am talking about the so-called government army.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know this either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, thank you very much for this answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there a problem, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I heard you thanking the witness for the question, and I saw on the screen that it was translated as --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really do thank. I have a two-fold thanks to say to all the interpreters. I did not commit a lapsus calami but a lapsus linguae. I just made a simple mistake in pronunciation. Thank you very much for correcting me to all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer, Witness. Later I will ask you more questions with respect to the time while you were a soldier. But I would now like to go on to -- pass on to another element of this cross-examination. I would like to talk about the document that you deciphered yesterday with a great deal of difficulty. It was the document that comprised two pages, and you will remember that this Chamber did not retain one portion of a paragraph because it was not legible. I believe that you remember this document. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If this answer -- thank you for this answer, Witness. Now, first question: Do you speak or do you read the English language?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this answer. Witness, did you ever get the chance before reading this document in Serbian to see or to hear from whatever source the English translation of this report that was made by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see the translation for that report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before hearing -- before actually reading the second page of this report, have you had a meeting with the representatives of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And during that meeting, is it possible that they have in some way refreshed your memory as to the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did hand me a copy of this document to read.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just checking something on the transcript, Mr. President, because my question was, was it possible that the document had refreshed your memory? And your response was "yes."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, am I correct in saying, Witness, that when you deciphered -- when you managed to make out this document with certain difficulty, the Defence had already refreshed your memory?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The translation that I just received is that the Defence had refreshed my memory. Is that the question that you asked?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may have misspoken, in which case I apologise. But I was, of course, referring to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it refreshed my memory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this seems to be my second slip, but I was saying this for the benefit of the Chamber because I wanted to make sure that the reading of the document took place only after witness's memory had been refreshed. I think he's having problems with his screen. If I may consult with my colleague for a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I'd like to put a question to the witness in view of the last observation you made.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, you have testified that the Prosecution refreshed your memory, and you have testified that you received, as far as I understand, in the original Serbian version the document. When you said that your memory was refreshed, did you mean to say that it was refreshed by receiving and rereading the document or by anything more, such as discussing the document with members of the investigation or Prosecution team? Could you explain to us what you understand by your memory being "refreshed"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said in order to refresh my memory, I meant in order to remember the details concerning the impact site, members of the team, and similar information. Because after all, this took place six years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But what I'd like to know is whether the refreshment of your memory was limited by receiving and reading the document, or that there was any further discussion on the content of the document with any person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I was simply given the text in the Bosnian language to read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise for saying "Serbian language." You correct me and say it's the Bosnian language. We usually says "B/C/S," which is Bosnian, Serbian, Croatian. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Concerning this issue, Mr. President - this is just a digression - personally, I do not appreciate the usage of the term B/C/S. It doesn't mean much. I know it is simple and convenient, but it doesn't really reflect the reality. It's a neologism.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking of the refreshing of your memory, Witness, can you tell us where exactly it took place? Where was it, in which office, that your memory was refreshed in this manner?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened during my last preparations here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, are we talking about the day of yesterday, that is, prior to your being asked questions about this particular exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I meant last week, when I arrived here upon invitation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but Witness, which language did you speak with the representatives of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke in English directly, without the assistance of an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpreter was present, but I didn't need his or her services.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. After you had refreshed your memory concerning this incident with the representatives of the OTP, did they speak about the contents of the report with you in English?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I simply read the document, and that was it. There was no further discussion about the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me now move on to a different subject of a more technical nature which concerns specifically the shelling of the Markale market. Witness, you testified yesterday at one point that the crater which was caused by the fall of the stabiliser, that is, the tunnel caused by the tail-fin, was some 9 centimetres long. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
