utterances.text: It was not 9 centimetres in diameter, but the length of the tunnel was 9 centimetres, together with the part of the tail-fin which was embedded in the surface and the one that was sticking out that could be seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to look at the transcript also, but what do you mean when you say damaged surface? What do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am referring to the asphalt surface of the portion of the ground hit by the shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, Witness, you're telling us that from the asphalt to the bottom of the crater, the distance is approximately 9 centimetres, that is, that the depth was approximately 9 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the depth was about 9 centimetres approximately, but the tail-fin was still inside the crater when we did our measurements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was in total the depth of the crater?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't take any measurements after the tail-fin had been extracted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling me that you did not take any measurements of the lower portion of the crater? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the UNPROFOR members took it out, took the tail-fin out, we did not take any measurements of the depth of the crater.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for clarity sake, we could perhaps give the witness a blank piece of paper so that he can explain to us the situation more easily, with your permission, of course. Thank you. And with the kind assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have a piece of blank paper in front of you. Could you draw the diagram on the ELMO so that we can all see what you're doing. We can switch to the appropriate channel in order to be able to follow you. Witness, let me allow you to give you some instructions. I think that you drew a horizontal line that represents the surface of the location. Are you going to give us a cross-section of the spot? Very well, thank you. So we are talking about a cross-section of the location. Will you please now draw for us the crater which was 9 centimetres deep. Can we have a cross-section of such a crater?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let me now ask you to do the following: I will look at the other screen so as to be able to follow you. On the horizontal line that you have just drawn, to the right of the horizontal line, would you please write letters "TN," which in French stands for "terrain naturel," which is a term used in architecture, that is, the natural ground. Since you are a technician by profession, will you please use the usual symbols, that is, the beginning of the measurement and the end of the -- just a second, please. Just a second, please. Thank you. On the left side of the diagram, that is, to the left of the centre of your diagram, will you please use the usual technical indication marks to indicate the measurements.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking about centimetres, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please indicate that next to the number.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My thanks to the interpreters. Mr. President, I don't know whether this document is going to be tendered, whether we will tender it, or if you prefer that I describe it for the record. We can always tender it later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you will tender it, of course it gets a number, D number, and otherwise, how would you like me -- is there any necessity of describing it? Otherwise, if it's not tendered, perhaps it could be marked identification. But I don't exactly understand what you asked me, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if there's an objection from the Prosecution concerning the tendering of this document, then I will describe it for the record. If as early as now we can agree that the document will be admitted into evidence, then there's no need for me to describe it for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's clear enough for the record that the witness is making, upon your instructions, sketches on a clean piece of paper. But that's already in the transcript. So please proceed. I didn't hear any objections until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, will you please try to do the same once again, that is, to indicate the same technical symbols underneath the artifact? To the left, yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, having drawn a cross-section of an artifact embedded in the ground, the witness has indicated, to the left of the line, the distance of 9 centimetres, which would indicate the superior portion of the crater, and the second one which also goes to the left but bears no specific markings. The second portion of the crater was never measured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the case, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't measure that portion. I think that it was Mr. Berko Zecevic who took such measurements later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure that Mr. Zecevic proceeded to that exercise, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not a hundred per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Still along the same lines with respect to the Markale market incident --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we can perhaps move the diagram from the ELMO, but we can indicate with an interrogation mark the other side of the sketch because we are not aware of the measurements. So I will ask the witness to mark the lower part of the drawing with an interrogation mark.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. To go back to the Markale market incident, another incident as well, but in particular to the Markale market incident, how did you establish technical measurements with respect to the topography, that is, what did you do in order to determine a point of impact with respect of some fixture like a wall or a building in the immediate vicinity?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the measurement tape which is part of the normal investigation kit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, was that the only technique which was used by all investigation teams, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including UNPROFOR personnel?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what is the error of margin - we have seen that there was a 5 degree margin of error in one such case - in cases of this method?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Plus or minus 5 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, at this point, I should like to show this witness a document. It is D68. We will check ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I was just wondering about the record or the transcript I have here, the answer to the last question, plus or minus 5 centimetres. I'm wondering if perhaps we could check the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it's useful to check it, because the answer in the French version was a bit different. It was something, but it's just my recollection, plus or minus 5 degrees, but then in centimetres. So I heard the word "centimetres" in French, but also "degree." So perhaps we'll have to check that, or perhaps ask for a clarification to the witness right away. If you could please do so, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It may have been a slip not made by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I have to ask you to rephrase your answer, or rather to repeat your answer. Didn't you say plus or minus 5 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, because we're talking about the distance between the crater and the familiar objects in the vicinity which is measured with a measuring tape, and it is expressed in centimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we are talking about the same figure, Witness. Thank you very much for this clarification. Do you remember, Mr. Sabljica, in your report, what the distance was between the impact point and the wall which was closest to it, to the impact point?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The closest object was the nearby shop which was located at a distance of 4 metres and 16 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You really have a technician's memory. These are indeed the numbers that we heard yesterday. And now I'm going to show you a document who, according to our new stamp, is D68.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document please be submitted to the witness. Let us perhaps wait a moment before we show the document to the witness. Mr. President, there seems to be a problem or ... ?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to avoid whatever misunderstanding that perhaps the witness already awaiting, whether you'll tender the document or not, already put his initials on the document. Otherwise someone might think that it was drawn by Mr. TN.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's my omission, Mr. President. Mr. Terra Naturale is, of course, not present. My apologise. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we please ask the witness to -- it's already on the -- I see that the initials are on the bottom right-hand corner. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if, however, an error in the positioning of the point of impact was committed, would that logically speaking have consequences on any relevant conclusion contained in the ballistics report?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the margin of error is very low, plus or minus 5 centimetres, I don't think that it would have seriously affected the findings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if, however, this margin of error was significantly higher, is it possible that the results of the investigation would have been significantly different?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about metres, then yes, such a mistake would have significantly affected the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, to your knowledge and to the best of your recollection, what was the distance which was measured by your team or yourself between a point of impact and the building which is referred to as the 22nd December building?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the distance was 11.6 metres, that is 11 metres and 60 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. These figures are on the exhibits that have been submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should now like to have the witness shown D68.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... D69.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that you would like to show a document to the witness which would be D68. And I think for that reason, Madam Registrar gave the sketch already D69. So that's what I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, I'm sorry, but there seems to be a confusion. The exhibit which we intend to produce now, it's a new exhibit. It's a diagram but not a diagram made by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, as indicated before, that would be D68. And for that reason, the registrar gave the sketch just drawn by the witness D69 in order to avoid whatever confusion. So Mr. Usher, would you then --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right, Mr. President. We will renumber our document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any reason? Did it have anything --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. Actually, we have pre-marked other exhibits with D68, so we will continue the same numbers, or maybe the registrar could assign D69 to this diagram so that the documents that we have pre-marked are not altered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you just now would hand over the document that you would like to show the witness to the usher, then we will see how it is pre-marked and we will find a solution. Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much in advance. For the record, Mr. President, let me indicate that this diagram bears an ERN number, 0026-409, and that it has been disclosed by the Prosecution. It is actually an investigation record compiled by I don't know whom. But it is a work product by UNPROFOR, D68.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you have in front of you the document which we see on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you see somewhere to the right side of the place which is represented by a very large square?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please read the numbers concerning the large shop which are expressed in metres on this document. The first one which indicates the big shop on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 6 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please remind us what your measurements were regarding this impact site?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 4.16 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. As for the other side, that is, the facade of the 22nd December building, that is the large building, for the record, which we can see on the right-hand side of the picture and which is higher than the one in front of it, what is the distance that you can see on this diagram?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 8 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. What was the distance that you indicated in your report?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, what is the height of the building that you can see here on the diagram, that is, the 22nd December building?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this diagram, 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. A moment ago, you told us that if the margin of error was expressed in metres, that that would affect the findings of your investigation. Can you confirm that once again?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I do confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further question with respect to this document. This document can be removed. The witness is not the author of this diagram. Unless you have any questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have one question. Perhaps we could put this diagram again, that's D68, on the ELMO. You asked, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, "Will you please read the numbers concerning the large shop which are expressed in metres on this document, the first one which indicates the high shop on the left-hand side." And then the witness's answer was "6 metres." Then your next question was: "Will you please remind us what your measurements were regarding this impact site?" Which is not a very precise question. And you, Mr. Sabljica, you answered, "4 metres, 16 centimetres." It is my recollection that the distance of 4 metres, 16 centimetres, was the distance from the impact up to the shop building. Were you referring to that distance when you answered the question of Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you were reading the indication on this indicating 6 metres, was that the distance between the impact and the building or is it the height of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the distance between the impact point and the building, as we can see here on this diagram.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that is not the left part of the shop building but the right part of the shop building. Is that true? Because the question referred to the left part of the building, which also indicates -- yes, we have now ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm terribly sorry. I do apologise. I believe what I said in French is the following: The left side of the buildings that are shown. With respect to the right side, which is the 22nd December building, this is what I meant. That's what I meant when I said "the left side of the buildings." In the diagram, in fact, that we're talking about, it's on the right-hand side of the building situated to the left. Do we agree on this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it has become quite clear to me now. You have seen, perhaps, that the left part of the building, there is also an indication of 6 metres, but that's different. So you are talking about the left building, but the right-hand side, the distance. It's clear to me. Thank you for assisting me in better comprehension of the testimony of the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with pleasure will I proceed, but I need the authorisation of interpreters, because I'm in some way between their kind hands. We do not have any transcript -- but I can see it did come back. I have just been told that the transcript came back. May I know if the transcript is back in all the booths?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, for the English transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I will then go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for answering these questions. You have told us a moment ago that your memory was refreshed in sorts. I will now submit to you a document, and I would like you to tell us if the two first pages of the said document were either written by yourself or, according to the instructions that you had given to someone, by someone else. I believe this is document D70. And Mr. Witness, I would like you to look at the first two pages only of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since we have placed these pages in the right order - we hope that we have stapled them in the right order - it will not be possible to have the whole document on the screen. So we will have to proceed step by step. Mr. Usher, would you be kind enough to place the first page of this document on the screen, the first page bearing the marking D70. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the same time, as we are looking at this document, Mr. Witness, would you please take the second page, place it on the ELMO for just a few seconds, and then we will go back to the first page. Very well. We now see that it is the second page following the first page. It's a complementary page, and I would like you to go back to the first page. [In English] And put it on the ELMO, thanks. [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Witness, would you please tell us if you recognise this document, or do you know of the existence of this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I see this document for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document was never shown to you at any point in time during no expertise?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So Witness, do you see before you on this first page a sketch representing on the right-hand side the building bearing the name 22nd of December, but we can only read the last word, "December," and that to the left, do you see the second building closing off that square? In other words, is this a sketch, or is this a diagram of the Markale square?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This seems to resemble the diagram of the Markale market.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. Would you please focus on the very small squares that we see at the centre of the picture. That is, on the space of the square itself, do you see those square boxes -- those rectangular boxes?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, tell us if you can, according to your knowledge of the scene, what would those small rectangles represent, aligned in such a fashion?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stalls of the market.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, according to your memory, the way the stalls are represented here, does this correspond to reality, the reality such as it was then on that market?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it seems to be represented in a very faithful fashion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this answer. Witness, can you tell us if every time we see a line or a row, do you mean that this is the row of stalls, the way they were at the time? They were all close together, in twos?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this was the case, yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, thank you very much. Would you be kind enough as to count for us the number of rows that we can see on this square? Would you please do it on the screen so that I can follow you as well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is counting.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are 18 rows.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for the transcript, I must say that we are talking about the second and the first page, so now I would like -- this document is comprised of two pages. So I would like the usher to put page number 2 on the ELMO. Please go back to page number 2 so that we can see the extension of this first page. We can see the ERN number, 0026-8362 on this page. This is therefore the second page following the first page. The first page bears an illegible ERN number, but this is a document which goes together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Witness, could you please tell us what does this word mean? There is a word at the centre of this picture, to the right.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shop. Samo Posluga.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we are talking about the supermarket that we have seen earlier on the previous diagram. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please confirm to us so that we are totally clear, that the arrow that is showing "S" means the north, or does "S" stand for "sjever," north?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you very much. I did this because with this document we have annexed a third page. It is a page that we have also received from the Prosecution. It may be seen the other way around. It's not really very important, but this is the document bearing the number 0026-8326. And I would like to ask the witness at this point to be so kind enough as to count the rows, the stalls, the stall rows that he sees on the square.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us how many stall rows were you able to count on this square?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven horizontal and one vertical, if we look at this picture from the position which I am in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, could you just please tell us if this is a diagram depicting the Markale square and where is, therefore, the Marsal Tito Street with respect to this square? Would you please show it to us? To your right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a diagram, yes. And this is Marsal Tito Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness showed with the pointer the horizontal lines that were located above the number ERN, and these lines close off the square. Thank you very much, Witness. I will not need this document any more. But for the transcript, Mr. President, I would just like to indicate that this was a document that was already submitted to your Chamber. While we heard the previous witness -- I will not mention the previous witness's name. It's for discretionary reasons, of course, but you will know who this witness was, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Please, now we are going to show you a videoclip. I have two cassettes in my possession. And I would like you, Witness, now more than ever to ask the kind assistance of the interpreters. Why, because the cassette that we are going to see, the videoclip, is in the Serbian language. I think it is quite difficult to hear the conversations. But I do thank the interpreters in advance. I know that their ear is very sharp, and I would kindly ask them to concentrate and focus on each word, and this is why I'm going to ask them to do the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will hand now these videocassettes to the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the interpreters wish to point out that we do not do any interpretation of videotape without transcript as a matter of principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I don't know whether you want to respond to the request of Mr. Piletta-Zanin or whether there's anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Two things: As a matter of practice, what we heard from the interpreters' booth, to my understanding, is correct. A transcript ought to be provided if we're going to refer to words on a tape. Second matter of practice, if a video and audiotape is going to be shown, it is normally given to the other side to examine before it is brought to Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just ask you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is the videotape that you're going to play one that comes from the Prosecution? So it is a replay of what we have seen before, or is it a ... ?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, last time we had this confusion, but unless I'm mistaken, this videocassette was provided to us by the Prosecution. I asked the case manager to give me a clearer copy. She was not able to do so unfortunately, so we've only copied some clips. We didn't want to waste any time by showing the whole videoclip that we have seen already. But these are excerpts from the V000-3274, copy number 4, video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me be very practical at this very moment, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. First of all, the interpreters are not able to translate any text spoken on a videotape if not -- if there's no transcript made available to them of what has been said. That would go beyond what they are supposed to do as interpreters, and that's what they object to. So if you would like to have parts of what has been said on a videotape be translated, you first have to provide the booth with a transcript. That's number 1. Number 2, I do understand that you made a new, as one would say in French, perhaps collage of parts that we have seen before. I think it will be fair -- you are nodding no. Please explain, if it's not a new compilation of videopictures we saw before, what exactly what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, no. Well, we have a problem -- two problems. The first one is resolved. Now, with your permission, we will see this videocassette and we will ask the witness to tell us what is it that he heard. He will then be able to say it out loud if he heard in his own language. And then if we have heard it, I suppose that the witness can hear it, and then the interpreters may interpret what the witness had said. I think that this clarifies this point. Now, the second thing, the excerpt in question was not seen -- the Chamber has not seen this excerpt. We have received many cassettes, videocassettes. This one is one of them. This is not a collage. This is not an edited version, it's an excerpt, but it has not been seen by the Chamber yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps since we'll have a break anyhow, and since I expect Mr. Ierace to be in the Court, I thought at 20 minutes past 12.00, so that before the next break we would have 10 minutes to explain to the Court what he had -- what he wished to explain to the Court, then I would suggest that during the break the Prosecution first views, if possible, this tape so that they can see whether they recognise it, whether they know what it is, and then see whether there's any objection against playing it. But is there any information as far as Mr. Ierace is concerned? Because I would have expected him to be here five minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I would imagine that he's on his way, but I have no new information to advise the Court on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but Mr. Ierace wanted to give his information. I would say let's just save the tape for after the break, and let's see what communication in 20 minutes could do. I know it's not a use of the break which everyone would prefer, but nevertheless let's see whether we can solve the problem during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just one short comment. Very well, but I would not like to be placed in a situation where, since I said yesterday that unfortunately I will not be able to be here tomorrow, and this is the reason why Mr. Ierace wanted to make his comment today, I didn't want the Defence to be handicapped in the presentation of its case. I mean, unfortunately, Mr. Ierace is late, and I did not want the Defence to suffer from this, because we are not responsible for the occurrence of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll take care the Defence will not suffer. Mr. Ierace, we have all been waiting for you. Seeing you enter the courtroom is a great pleasure for all of us. Mr. Sabljica, your cross-examination will be resumed after the break, but we'll first hear, for five or ten minutes, other things. So could the booth please take care that Mr. Sabljica is not on the picture when he's escorted out of the courtroom. Yes, please. Mr. Ierace, could you be as brief as possible. As you know, we usually have the break at half past 12.00, and we only have three minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I apologise for that, Mr. President. In relation to the orders, in particular the specific questions that you posed on Tuesday, we may have documents in our possession which fall under those two categories, in part because various parts of the OTP are constantly receiving material. The search that will take place on the 25th of March will cover most of that material, and by early April we will be able to inform the Defence of any further relevant material that we have by way of orders that come under those two descriptions that you gave on Tuesday. Last night, at 20 to 11.00, the Defence faxed to the Prosecution a further request for orders and documentation of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This request included documentation that refers to the formation of that army, and the acting and planning of military actions of the general staff of the army. Mr. President, I do not intend to disclose material that we have, if any, in relation to the formation of the army because it is not within Rule 66 of the Tribunal. In other words, it's not, as far as I can see, material to the Defence. But I wish to make this more fundamental point: I informed the Trial Chamber that there was a mission to the -- which gave us access to the archives of the army early last year. And that yielded many hundreds of documents, all of which have been disclosed to the Defence in the form of an index, and the Defence were invited to nominate which documents they wanted, and they were provided. Mr. President, that archive consisted of hundreds of thousands of documents which related to the 1st Corps. The mission confined itself to documents which related to the particular brigades in the areas of the scheduled incidents. That alone took six staff members of the OTP ten days. Any exculpatory material which was found during that search was included in the index provided to the Defence. So it is physically impossible for the Prosecution to go back and search through hundreds of thousands of documents and to make those indeed available to the Defence, which is the terms of its present request. That is not the job of the Prosecution. The Defence can make its own approach if it thinks it appropriate to the relevant authorities and seek access to those archives. So Mr. President, in short, in order to -- for the OTP to be satisfied that no further documents have come into its possession which are material to the Defence, we are undertaking a further search, and we'll have the results of that by early April. In relation to the shrapnel, I understand my friend raised that issue again this morning. On Tuesday, I said I would report back next week, but I can do so now. A written request was made by the OTP on the 28th of August of last year for the shrapnel in relation to the Markale incident on the 5th of February, 1994. We were advised by the relevant authorities that they no longer had the shrapnel. There is nothing more that we can do to locate the shrapnel. We have approached the relevant authorities; they no longer have it. And as far as the OTP is concerned, that is the end of the matter in terms of searching for those pieces. The reason the approach was made then was this: It followed on some earlier approaches made mid-last year, and that was in pursuance of a general policy that artifacts remain within the possession of the Bosnian government authorities until such time as they are required for the trial. Given the trial timetable, we thought it appropriate in mid-2001 to secure the relevant artifacts. Mr. President, the only other issue that I would seek to raise very briefly is Robert Donia. I notice that the Defence has filed some material this morning in relation to experts saying that they speak 20 days' notice before the calling of experts. The Defence -- the Prosecution, rather, proposes to call Robert Donia at some point on or after the 22nd of April, and of course that is well in excess of 20 days' notice. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace, for your information. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, when we come back after the break, I would like to address the Court with two issues. There are some things that cannot be left up in the air, but of course everybody has the right to a break. So I will, with your leave, address the Court after the break with two issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether it will be done right after the break or just at the end of the morning session, we'll decide that. You see, one of the advantages is that if there's limited time, it's our experience that things usually are dealt with in a more efficient way. We'll now have a break until 5 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for giving me the floor, Mr. President. I think we have reasons for optimism because the parties have just reached an agreement. We will try to finish the examination of the witness, and Mr. Ierace and myself have reached the conclusion that, with the Court's permission, we can respond to this intervention on Monday later, after the morning session, once we have viewed the hearings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we'll hear, then, from you on Monday. That also means that we could now continue the cross-examination of the witness. Mr. Usher, would you please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, two tapes have been provided to the Prosecution. They have not made any protest so far. I don't know whether Mr. Ierace is raising in order to object -- no. It seems that he is leaving. I knew it. May we please now give these tapes to the booth. Mr. Stamp is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed that. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We received two tapes from the Defence, and we did what we could in the time allowed to have a look at them. The tape which I believe my friend proposes to hand to the booth to be played has material on it which I cannot conceive of it bearing any relevance to this case and is not in either of the tapes which have been played before or produced in Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say you object at least partially to the relevance. Let's -- could you indicate when we come to those points and when we have perhaps entered in those areas, because if you say, "now comes the part of the tape which is irrelevant," of course we have got no idea what will then come. And if there's any general remark, Mr. Piletta-Zanin is aware of the points which you think the tape is irrelevant?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I haven't had an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that 20 minutes is not much time. Let's just proceed, I would say, and if you indicate whenever we come to a point. And sometimes, even if a small part of the tape would not be that relevant but would not harm the case of the Prosecution -- I know that 45 seconds irrelevant material, although it should not be there, under circumstances might to be preferred above 5 minutes of discussion on relevance of the 45 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed. In the interests of time, we could proceed, though the second thing I wish to add is we did not have time to compare what we got with our originals. But we could proceed in the interests of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could we have a number for the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The tape is with Mr. Usher. It has not been marked with a number yet, but I think that the number would be 72. We already have 71. 7-2. Thank you. Let me indicate, Mr. President, that I have not had the opportunity of viewing the tape which has been handed over to me by the relevant authorities, but I know that it is an excerpt of a tape which was provided to us by the Prosecution and that the tape is familiar to the Prosecution because that's where it originates from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, unless you come up with another D71, the last one we have is D70, which is the three-page well-stapled sketch, two different sketches, of what the witness testified is the Markale market. So if it's D71 -- you're nodding. That means that the tape will be D71?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document -- the one that we are tendering is D71. But they have been premarked, these documents. That is why the tape is going to be 72. We have an image on the screen now, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But before we view the tape, and I will give the instructions in English, I should like to ask the witness that he listens carefully to the words spoken on the tape.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now view the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] Do we have any problem with the tape recorder?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we stop here, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have just heard a passage on this tape. I think it was perfectly audible. I hope you have heard the words yourself, or maybe do you wish to have the tape replayed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, thank you, I have heard the text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what you have just heard, the words that you have just heard spoken by an individual on this tape?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Please have a look at the roof, the tail-fin may be there."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is precisely what was said on the tape. Thank you very much for the quality of that quote, Witness. So at the time they were initially inspecting the scene, the investigators were wondering whether the stabiliser or the tail-fin could be found on the roof. Is that correct? Is that the meaning of the passage that we have just heard?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I know whose voice it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the owner of the voice is?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The voice comes from Sead Besic, the crime technician.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, when we hear this reference to the roof, is it the roof of the 22nd December building? Is that the roof in question?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, why would a tail-fin end up on a roof? Why would it be found on a nearby roof?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why Mr. Besic said that, since we later found the stabiliser in the centre of the crater.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is a crucial element, and words were spoken to the effect that it can be found on the roof. Don't you find it strange that such an important item can be found on the roof?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not standing near the camera when he was speaking. It's just that I recognised his voice only now from the tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions regarding this tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have another tape that I would like to have the witness view, just a very brief passage. Can we see the same passage again for a few seconds, please. For the transcript, the tape that we have just seen concerns the Markale market incident, the time being the time of the inspection of the surrounding area of the crater.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next tape will, of course, be 73, number 73. I indicate this to Madam Registrar. I don't know if we have the image on the screen yet, whether the technicians are ready. We will proceed pursuant to their orders. I don't have an image on my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just wait, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. If there are any technical problems from the booth, I'd like to know. Otherwise, we'll just wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am informed that it takes some time to change the tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem, Mr. President. Meanwhile, let us take the opportunity of the availability of Mr. Usher, who will please help us distribute this document, D71, to the witness. We will save time by proceeding in this manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, while we wait for the technical problems to be resolved --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wait for one second to provide it to the witness. If the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can perfectly see the image on the screen now. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the counsel because of the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We don't hear the counsel at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I do not think that the interpreters are able to -- can translate you and at the same time there's a lot of noise for us also to understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to give any instructions to the witness, please do it prior to playing the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Mr. President. I thought it was possible. I just wanted to save time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, simply the following: Would you please pay attention to two things regarding the next tape, and that is the position of the arrows on the surface with respect to the surrounding buildings and also the location of the 22nd December building with respect to the road which is on the opposite side of Marsal Tito Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we continue with the viewing, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have the cassette replayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we stop here, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, as regards this image, can you confirm that the central crater is covered with debris?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this yellow material, yellow traces that we see?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean specifically what is in the centre of the image at the bottom of the image, slightly above the white pole which is positioned diagonally in this image. Can you confirm that in the centre, bottom centre, of this image, we can see the crater?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you also confirm that the crater is completely covered with debris and soil?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot. It doesn't seem to be covered to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you see here a hole or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see a hole at the very bottom of the image next to the white tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, as regards this surrounding area, the one which is bordered with white chalk, was this area cleared, was it cleaned up?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are certain traces left. There is still some soil or sand on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate for us the tail-fin on this image? Can you give us an objective assessment of this?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Objectively speaking, I don't see it at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you read the date indicated on this image? It should be found in the bottom left corner of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. February the 6th --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we have difficulties in following your questions on the centre of the image where there's supposed to be a hole because it's just beyond our screen where one would expect the centre of what might be a crater is. Could you, please, either by moving forward or backwards, give us a better image --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We can perhaps ask the technicians to go back a little bit. But -- to zoom back a little bit, but I think that the orifice or the hole that I was talking about is perfectly visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a little more to the back, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this will do, thank you. Mr. President, I think that the hole we mentioned now is now more visible. I don't know whether it is visible for you. It depends, of course, on the quality of this image.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, one last question for the sake of clarity: The orifice at the bottom part of the crater was not measured, that is, the area which is underneath the black area which is in the bottom of the image that we can now see on the screen. Was that the case?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me ask the technicians to speed up a little bit so that we can proceed with further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Moving forwards?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, of course. Will you please do that? [Interpretation] Can we fast forward, please. [In English] Could you please accelerate the speed? [Interpretation] Because I'm not sure that everything was reproduced on the tape. Can we stop here. Thank you. Can we now have the normal speed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well. It goes on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This is the end of the tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we were able to distinguish the arrows which were drawn on the surface, on the ground, that is. Is it true -- just a second, please. These arrows slightly point towards the 22nd December building. Was that the case, according to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my recollection and in view of what I have just seen, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, we have just viewed this tape. It is going to be tendered into evidence. Can you now tell us whether the 22nd December building extends all the way to the street which is situated opposite Marshal Tito Street, that is, on the other edge of the market where we were able to see an alley, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no further questions regarding these tapes, but I do have a few questions regarding this witness's military activity, or actually military activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us if there is a technique difference in what we call in military art unfortunately a shell and a mine? Do you know what the difference between the two is?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very briefly, Witness, would you be able to point out the difference to us?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I know, mines are devices that can destroy the enemy lines. It's these explosives. Whereas shells are projectiles that are fired, and it's artillery projectiles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Witness, you lived through the war. What was going on during the fighting in respect to fuel? How was the army able to obtain fuel supplies?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I really do not know what the case was for the army, but I do know what was going on in the police when we had to move and go to on-site investigations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So therefore, could you tell us how is it that the police was able to get fuel?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a logistics service of the MUP, and they were in charge of this. So we would receive one litre per investigation for a car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the reason being that fuel was not regularly available on the open market. Is that the right reason?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, with respect to that period in which the war took place, is it possible that some vehicles, to your knowledge, civilian vehicles, would also be used by the army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but in that case, they had particular stickers that would identify them as being members of the army. They were not painted in a camouflage manner, but they bore certain distinction signs, emblems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What were those stickers, briefly?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The former emblem of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was four -- it was the coat of arms, the fleur-de-lys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And since the Chamber may ask you about the size of these emblems, can you tell us what was the size of these emblems, of these stickers, to your recollection, according to your recollection, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say 30 by 40 centimetres on the hood and also on the doors of the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, have you heard of the existence of a mobile unit that was -- that had small mortars that were attached to civilian vehicles?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. And lastly, Witness, to the best of your recollection, what would be, if you can tell us, the definition of what we call a sniper?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, and I would have one last question for you, and I will ask you this question because you do read English. I would like to submit to the witness D71. You will receive this document from the usher in a few moments, and on this document, which is a two-page document, you will see under (a), under Item (a) for the date of the 22nd of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is the Annex number 6 of the final report of the UNPROFOR, and I would like the witness to read, if he is able to do so, the first paragraph that the witness has before him. And would you please place this on the ELMO, please. On the ELMO, so that everybody can follow. Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, do I understand you well that you are referring to Annex 6 to the report of the committee of experts?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that is the case. It is the same series of document, Annex 6, that is so, page seven hundred and -- my copy is quite illegible. 768 and 769.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you please read what appears under Item 22 for the 21st of January, 1994, under item (a), the first paragraph? Could you please read this.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, under military activity?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Combat and shelling activity: UNPROFOR reported that during the day, 40 SL were fired by Bosnian Serb forces, while 3 were fired by BH forces. 42 source, Agence France Presse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. One word is illegible, and that is not your fault, of course, and you can't do anything about it. Maybe we can read s-h-o-t. I'm just extrapolating here, but I believe that the meaning is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. There are no further questions. Mr. President, this puts an end to the cross-examination of this witness, and we thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. May I just indicate - I have not checked it - but "shells" also start with SH. So I don't know whether we can immediately follow you that it should be read "shot." Is there any need to re-examine the witness, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just a couple in clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. Re-examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at some of these documents that were shown to you by my learned friend. First, the one marked Defence Exhibit 68. Have you ever seen that document before today?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw this document for the first time today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you have a look at the one marked D70. The diagrams in that -- on the pages of that document, did you prepare those diagrams?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave some distances from your memory in respect to the measurements at the Markale incident in answer to my learned friend. Would you be able to say that the measurements which you took and which are a part of the document which you created yourself, are they accurate measurements in respect to that place?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I can confirm it with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could the witness have a look at P2307. I beg your pardon, P2309. I'm so sorry. Thanks, madam. While the registrar is finding it, may I just indicate that in the course -- remind the Court, in the course of the testimony, there had been some problems with legibility of a part of a document, and we had brought the original which turned out to be legible. I would like to distribute to the Court and to my learned friends copies of the original which are more legible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good copies of the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good copies of the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I just finished the cross-examination. May I ask Mr. Stamp if he found these documents in the last 10 seconds or if he was in possession of these documents while I was cross-examining? I believe that there is a loyalty question, one has to be loyal with regards to debates and fair, and I believe this is at least the least we can do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the document that has been distributed now by Mr. Stamp was not legible solely, I would say, on the agenda under number 3, which in the original we all have seen was about market stalls. I think there is nothing else more legible on this document than on the earlier copy of it. So please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Document P2309A?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm really terribly sorry, but could we also get a copy to make sure? We would like to see that sentence correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course. I expect you to get a copy as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But we do not have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I'll give you my copy just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Terribly sorry, sincerely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the record, in front of the witness is Exhibit P2309, which I believe my friends have in their possession. And that is what I'm asking the witness about. 9A, 2309A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at the penultimate page of this -- sorry, could you look at the page with the number 0026-8360 where you have drawn a diagram. The building numbered 5 on your diagram is the 22nd of December building?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were shown a video during cross-examination in which -- and you were asked about the arrow which was pointing towards the 27th of December building -- 22nd of December building, yes. Now, is the arrow that you saw in that video consistent with what you have in your diagram?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is that arrow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present at the investigation of the 6th of February?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in answer to my learned friend that Sead Besic had indicated that perhaps you could -- one could look at the roof to find the stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what he said. That's what we heard on the tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. When you came to the scene, the impact scene, at Markale, was it immediately apparent to you that the stabiliser was embedded in the ground?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what was the situation in respect to Mr. Besic? Do you know if Mr. Besic immediately was able to determine whether or not the stabiliser was buried in the ground?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to him and his knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you said the crater was 9 centimetres deep, that is 9 centimetres from the top of the asphalt.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is there a distinction between a crater and a tunnel that might be created by a stabiliser fin if it embeds itself in the ground?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about a softer surface?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A surface such as the one at Markale.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stabiliser was found at the centre of the crater at a depth of 9 centimetres from the asphalt surface.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that 9 centimetres which you speak of, does that 9 centimetres include the depth to which the stabiliser had embedded itself in the ground?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is the depth from the top of the asphalt up until the last part of the stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I have nothing further of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. May I just ask the interpreters booth, if there would be one or more, two questions of the Judges, whether we could continue for a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. Judge El Mahdi has a question or several questions for you. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Questioned by the Court: JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Witness, please tell me the following: Can you tell me what went on during the on-site investigation that you carried out regarding the Markale market incident. My first question relates to what you have said regarding Mr. Besic. You said that he, himself, had cleaned up the site. Did he carry out this cleaning up before or after you were able to determine the direction from which the shell was fired? Because if I understood you correctly, it was very important, in order to determine the trajectory, to be able to examine the debris to see where -- how scattered they are and at what distance they are from the point of impact. So if I understood correctly, he proceeded to the cleaning up of the site, but was this before or after attempting to try to determine the origin of fire and the direction from which the projectile landed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Besic proceeded to clean up the site of the artillery shell fall after only we established the parameters because the traces were very clear, very clean. And after we've established that the tail-fin was embedded in the crater and was at the centre of the explosion, Mr. Besic then proceeded to clean up more in detail the site in order to wait for the UNPROFOR team, who then delodged or extracted the tail-fin. This is why I mentioned that Mr. Besic proceeded to the cleaning up of the site. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you. And one short question: I'm just wondering here, you stated - and I will actually quote you in English - "... with the stabiliser which was lodged while awaiting the arrival of the UNPROFOR members." [Interpretation] How can you explain this? Do you usually proceed in this manner, in this fashion? Do you not usually extract the stabiliser? What do you usually do?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In cases such as the one at the Markale market where there were lots of casualties, lots of deaths, we did not wish to continue the work because the magistrate, the investigating magistrate, told us to stop and wait because the UNPROFOR members might come. We weren't really sure that they will or that they would come. So this was part of our usual procedure during the war. Whenever there was a greater number of civilian casualties, this is the way we were proceeding because usually the UNPROFOR was going on site as well in those cases. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, am I right in understanding that your method with the compass and the map requires the centre of the needle to be put precisely on the spot where the impact took place?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the circumstances permit so, yes, in order to be as precise as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How did you manage to get the centre of the needle of the compass on a rather large-scale map, as I can see, to be precise on the spot of the impact? I'm just trying to imagine for myself how to do it, look under it. How did you manage to get it exactly on the spot?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not exactly the spot, but we try to do our best in view of the kind of map that we have. In the case of Markale, the compass was located on the spot that I indicated in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you ever make an analysis of what would be the deviation if, for example, you'd put the centre of the needle, well, let's say 5 millimetres off the spot? I mean, what would that mean for the final result of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That kind of analysis was never done; however, the late Mr. Zlatko Medjedovic carried out similar analysis by using metal objects and testing them against this compass needle. We made sure that in the vicinity of the compass and the map that there were no metal objects which might have a more significant impact on the movements of the compass needle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did understand that, that you removed whatever metal objects there were. But especially analysis of what would be the effect on the outcome of your investigation if, for example, the centre of the needle would be 5 millimetres away from the exact spot of the impact on the map, because it's so difficult to look under the compass.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we never carried out such analysis. Personally, I don't think that 5 millimetres would be a significant deviation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sabljica. This concludes an examination of you as a witness, which lasted for a few days even, with some interruptions. You will be aware that it's of great importance for this Court, for this Chamber, to hear the answers of those who were present at the relevant times and places, the answers to the questions put by both parties and by the Judges themselves. It's important for us for the decisions we'll finally have to make. We are also aware that it's quite an effort for you to come from far away, travel to The Hague, stay here for I would say a few days, but perhaps even many days by now. So we would like to thank you very much that you have come to The Hague, that you have testified in this Court. And we'll wish you a safe journey home again. Mr. Usher, could you please lead the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Madam Registrar we should start tomorrow morning with the documents, since we asked already so much time from the interpreters. So I prefer to do that tomorrow morning first thing. And I think some of the documents, if they are admitted, will have to be admitted under seal because of the name of the protected witness on it. Then I would like to urge the parties, especially for tomorrow, to be again as efficient as possible. We know that those witnesses we are not able to examine tomorrow, if we are not able to conclude their examination, that they will have to wait for more than a week and either travel back or forth. So may I urge the parties to be as efficient as possible.
